The Uttar Pradesh state government has announced a major policy update regarding the recruitment of approximately 17,740 Trained Graduate Teacher (TGT) vacancies across 4512 government-aided secondary schools. Under the latest directives, the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) has been made a mandatory qualification for TGT positions for the first time. Alongside this requirement, authorities have introduced a conditional application window, allowing eligible candidates to apply and secure placement while extending the final deadline to pass the qualifying exam.

According to the official notification issued by Dr. Ashok Kumar Kannaujiya, Special Secretary, to the Secretary of the Uttar Pradesh Education Services Selection Commission, candidates have been granted time until June 30, 2027, to successfully clear the required TET exam and obtain a valid certificate.

Conditional Eligibility and Application Rules

The newly introduced guidelines alter how applicants approach the application process for the upcoming TGT vacancies:

  • Extended Passing Window: Applicants who have not yet cleared the mandatory TET exam are permitted to apply for the TGT posts, provided they fulfill the requirement and secure a valid certificate on or before June 30, 2027.
  • Conditional Appointments: Initial selection and inclusion in the merit list do not guarantee a permanent job appointment. Final confirmation remains strictly contingent upon fulfilling the TET qualification requirement within the stipulated timeframe.

According to administrative explanations, the timeline relaxation was granted because amending existing service rules and organizing a fresh TET exam requires an estimated minimum of three months. To prevent procedural delays in publishing the notification for the 17,740 TGT posts ahead of upcoming state elections, the government opted to implement this phased compliance window.

Additional Updates for Teaching Aspirants

Alongside the TGT announcement, the state government addressed recruitment criteria for other educational positions. Following directives from the Supreme Court, the maximum age limit for Shikshamitras participating in the recruitment drive for 11,508 Assistant Teacher posts in municipal areas has been relaxed to 60 years. Meanwhile, standard age criteria for general candidates applying for teaching positions remain set between 21 and 40 years as of July 1.

Practical Implications and Verification

For candidates preparing for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh teaching drives, balancing subject-specific preparation with general pedagogical requirements is essential. While TGT selection relies heavily on specialized knowledge in disciplines such as Mathematics, Science, Social Studies, and Languages, candidates must also clear the broader TET syllabus before the June 2027 deadline.

  • Confirmed Facts: The state has cleared 17,740 TGT posts in government-aided secondary schools, made TET mandatory for these roles, and established a final compliance deadline of June 30, 2027. Shikshamitras have been granted an age relaxation up to 60 years for primary recruitment.
  • Unknowns: Exact dates for the opening and closing of the official online application window, detailed exam schedules, and the specific date of the upcoming TET examination have not been finalized in the initial notification.
  • How to Verify: Readers can review the complete official notification details and updates directly through the Jagran Josh Official Source.
